title: Former FIFA Council member Isha Johansen calls on Gianni Infantino to step down
dek: Isha Johansen, ex-FIFA Council member and former Sierra Leone FA president, publicly called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign over ethical breaches in the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal. Johansen invoked Infantino's own 2021 advice to her about stepping down for the good of football. CAF's executive committee has unanimously backed Infantino for re-election in 2027, but dissent from African football figures is growing.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Johansen told ESPN that Infantino's actions with the FIFA Forward Enterprise 'crossed an ethical line' and 'led to a breakdown of trust in his leadership that may now be beyond repair,' per ESPN reporting.
bottom_line: Johansen's public dissent marks the first prominent African football figure to break with continental consensus on Infantino, signaling fractures in a coalition that has so far been his strongest institutional support. What to watch: whether other African FA leaders follow Johansen's lead, and whether CAF's unified stance holds as domestic political pressure on member nations intensifies over the rejected $40 million offer.
body: Isha Johansen, a former FIFA Council member and ex-president of the Sierra Leone Football Association, publicly called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign, citing ethical breaches in the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal and breaking from the unified African continental support that has so far insulated him from calls for his ouster.

Johansen served as SLFA president until 2021, when she withdrew from re-election three months after her March 2021 FIFA Council election, citing the demands of her new international responsibilities. According to ESPN, Johansen states that Infantino personally advised her at that time to step down, visiting Sierra Leone with CAF president Patrice Motsepe and telling her to resign "because it's a no win situation, and for the good of football." Johansen is now invoking that same logic against Infantino himself, saying she stepped down because he "stood by me because I was enforcing FIFA code of ethics, good governance, which is what FIFA supposedly stands for," and is calling on him to apply the same standard to his own position.

The FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, per ESPN's reporting, envisaged creating a commercial subsidiary valued at about $20 billion with a minority stake available to outside investors, up to 20%, and would have consolidated major FIFA revenue sources including broadcasting, sponsorship, and ticketing into the new entity. FIFA told its 211 member associations they could receive as much as $40 million each during the 2027-30 cycle if the plan proceeded. Johansen told ESPN that when she heard the proposal, she said, "this is a no deal. It's a no-go," describing Infantino's actions as crossing "an ethical line" and leading to "a breakdown of trust in his leadership that may now be beyond repair."

The proposal drew fierce opposition from UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation over both its substance and the process by which it was presented. Infantino subsequently withdrew the proposal and apologized. However, CAF's executive committee has unanimously backed Infantino and his re-election in 2027, with CAF president Motsepe publicly defending him on the basis of loyalty, describing the FIFA president as a loyal friend to Africa and saying that where he comes from, people do not "stab" those who have been loyal to them "in the back," according to ESPN.

Johansen emphasized that her opposition is "not about Gianni himself" but "about the act, the deed, the ethics behind the proposal. How it was presented, how it was unethical." She also highlighted the political bind facing African FA presidents: those who reject the $40 million offer face domestic consequences, because leaders "will have to explain how he managed, how it came about, how he worked that mathematics out to lose it. He will now lose face. His support base will also come after him and he will not get re-elected," per ESPN's account.

Musa Bility, former Liberia Football Association president and former CAF executive committee member, has also called on CAF to reconsider its endorsement, warning that "Africa must not become the firewall protecting one man from accountability," according to ESPN. UEFA is leading the charge among confederations demanding Infantino step down. According to ESPN's reporting, Infantino has gone from being a shoo-in for re-election to potentially being forced out or facing a challenge at the 2027 elections.
